sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Arabidopsis thaliana, thale cress, is a small annual of the mustard family, native across much of Eurasia and North Africa. Its rosette is only a few centimetres wide; flowering stems often reach about 10–30 cm, though conditions affect size. Tiny white flowers and slender seed pods suit the delicate scale of the plate.

sections.title: Why it is studied
sections.text: Its short life cycle, small genome and ease of cultivation made it a major model in genetics and developmental biology; its genome was the first plant genome to be fully sequenced. It is not a crop or a miniature snapdragon.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: No meaningful food use was verified for this profile; do not treat a research model or wild plant as an edible salad green without species-specific evidence.
